title: Voltage: start with L2
points: Study one synthetic feeder. The command controls fleet active and reactive participation.
Your task: check feasibility first, then compare the current-step objective.
note: The feeder is a synthetic SMART-DS Greensboro-area example, not a measured utility circuit. The default backend models MV phases and MV line currents, with idealized LV aggregation. Run L0 and L1 before this cell.
caption: Synthetic SMART-DS feeder model used by the voltage example; not an operational utility circuit.

title: Read the control and limits
points: a sets active-power participation; b sets reactive-power participation.
The notebook checks the inverter bounds, modeled voltage range and allowed current.
note: The command uses P_i = a S_i and Q_i = b S_i. Its bounds are 0 <= a <= 1, |b| <= 0.44 and a^2 + b^2 <= 1. Modeled voltage bounds are 0.95 to 1.05 p.u. RATING_FRACTION=0.80 sets the allowed current to 80% of the nominal rating. The displayed current percentage uses that reduced allowance as its denominator. Passing the inverter bounds alone does not establish network feasibility.
caption: Teaching diagram of the model or check used at this notebook step.

title: Run L2 with the default inputs
points: Run the whole L2 cell. It solves MPC, evaluates the saved SAC proposal and checks both.
Find feasible, current_step_J and max_allowed_current_pct in the output.
note: Start with LOAD_SCALE=1.0 and RATING_FRACTION=0.80. The saved SAC actor produces a new proposal by inference; it is not trained in this cell. Both proposals pass the default classroom checks. MPC has the lower current-step J for this case and objective. This single result does not establish a universal control advantage.

title: Read your voltage plots
points: Left: compare the sorted modeled voltage distributions with the allowed band.
Right: compare current use with the 100% allowed-current line.
note: The left panel sorts each voltage curve separately. The same horizontal position means the same rank, not necessarily the same physical bus. The right panel reports current relative to the reduced allowance. Use the output table for exact extrema and feasibility; do not decide acceptance from a plot alone.
caption: Actual executed notebook output; source cell classroom-007. Fresh numerical calculation unless explicitly marked archived.

title: Read feasibility before cost
points: Default MPC: PASS, current use 73.62%, current-step J about 0.03110.
Default saved SAC: PASS, current use 51.68%, J about 0.43643.
note: In the reference execution, MPC returns a=0.960307 and b=-0.111114, with Vmin=1.023874 and Vmax=1.038709 p.u. SAC returns a=0.340066 and b=0.014024, with Vmin=1.013243 and Vmax=1.030000 p.u. Values may vary slightly with the solver or dependency version. Lower current use need not mean lower J, because the objective also includes service and control terms. Check feasibility before comparing J.
caption: Actual executed notebook output; source cell classroom-007. Fresh numerical calculation unless explicitly marked archived.

title: Exercise 1: tighten the current allowance
points: In L2, change only RATING_FRACTION from 0.80 to 0.75. Predict, then rerun L2.
For each method, report feasible, allowed-current use and current_step_J.
Does passing this check establish full MV/LV feasibility? Explain your answer.
note: Allow one minute to predict, two minutes to edit and run, and one minute to report. Keep LOAD_SCALE=1.0. Reference allowed-current use is 78.527895% for MPC and 54.854158% for SAC; both remain feasible. Do not ask learners to find a rejection that this edit does not produce. The default model still covers MV only.

title: Debrief: a tighter allowance can still pass
points: At 0.75, both candidates still pass: MPC about 78.53%, SAC about 54.85%.
A stricter allowance raises utilization here, but it does not force a failure.
note: An incorrect prediction is useful evidence, not a failed exercise. Compare the hypothesis with the actual output. Both candidates retain enough headroom in this case. An optimizer may change its command when a constraint changes, so a simple fixed-ratio argument does not apply to every scenario. The model scope has not expanded.

title: Reset L2 before the recorded-choice lesson
points: Restore the default values and rerun L2 to keep your baseline easy to reproduce.
L3–L5 use the original test_01 context. They do not inherit your edited L2 experiment.
note: Make the experiment boundary explicit. L3 loads a separate preserved context into pool. It does not inherit the fresh L2 case or the participant's edits. Do not pair an edited L2 result with the test_01 model explanation as though the model had seen those new inputs.

title: L3 starts a separate recorded context
points: Run L3. Read the original context ID, model operations and recorded seconds.
The displayed reasons were recorded earlier. Opening them makes no new model call.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L3; cell classroom-010; archived test_01 context.
note: The output contains three actual replies from the frozen response-selection study. Ask learners to identify the operation and numerical parameters requested by each reply. The reported seconds measure the original model calls, not today's display cell. Keep this archived context separate from the fresh L2 comparison.

title: What did the language models choose?
points: Different wording can request the same tool and parameters.
The notebook groups identical physical trials; an explanation does not prove feasibility.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L3; cell classroom-010; archived test_01 context.
note: The three recorded replies reduce to two distinct canonical operations. The vote retains one contribution per model identity. In test_01, the Q-relaxation trial receives two votes. This diagram represents the archived input; it is not a new vote after a learner edits L2.
caption: Teaching diagram of the model or check used at this notebook step.

title: Run L4: check the recorded choice again
points: Run L4 after L3. Python performs a fresh numerical check on the original selected candidate.
Compare majority vote with frozen LinUCB on the same original context.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L4; cell classroom-013; fresh checks of archived choices.
note: The selector is frozen and makes no training updates in this lesson. L4 applies the archived selected operation to its original test context and runs a fresh numerical check. This is a replay with new verification, not a new language-model decision or an online learning experiment.

title: Separate the old choice from the new check
points: Both selectors choose the same Q-relaxation trial and pass the fresh MV check.
The predicted reward is not a feasibility result; read new_check_passes.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L4; cell classroom-013; fresh checks of archived choices.
note: The reference J is about 0.031082 for both selectors. The predicted reward is around -0.0075. It is a learned score, not a feasibility flag. Read new_check_passes for the engineering result. This one case does not show that learned selection is better than voting.
caption: Actual executed notebook output; source cell classroom-013. Fresh numerical calculation unless explicitly marked archived.

title: Run L5: identify the model scope
points: Leave RUN_OPENDSS=False and run L5. Read both the table and optional_mode message.
This checks the archived test_01 MV-MPC incumbent, with OpenDSS disabled.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L5; cell classroom-016; MV-only default model.
note: L5 reconstructs the original test_01 context and freshly checks its archived MV-MPC incumbent. This is not the Q-relaxation candidate checked in L4. With RUN_OPENDSS=False, it checks only the reduced model and reports that OpenDSS is disabled. It produces no fresh full-feeder audit in this CPU route. A separate recorded broader-model study is not a result calculated today.

title: A PASS belongs to the model that produced it
points: The default output checks MV phases and current. It does not cover all LV equipment.
If the request needs full MV/LV coverage, request a broader-model check or HOLD.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L5; cell classroom-016; MV-only default model.
note: Ask a participant to read the explicit scope message aloud. A PASS is conditional on the model and action that were checked. The default model does not cover every LV constraint. A more confident explanation cannot supply the missing model coverage.
caption: Actual executed notebook output; source cell classroom-016. Fresh numerical calculation unless explicitly marked archived.

title: Voltage checkpoint: state exactly what ran
points: L2: fresh MPC and saved-policy proposals. L3: old model replies. L4–L5: fresh checks of test_01.
Report the input, candidate, model scope and outcome before proposing the next step.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L5; cell classroom-016; MV-only default model.
note: Give pairs 30 seconds to describe the sequence without calling every step an AI decision. L2 calculates proposals for the current classroom inputs. L3 displays archived replies, L4 rechecks selected trials, and L5 checks the archived incumbent's model scope. Numerical tools provide the physical evidence; the bounded model choice selects a permitted trial. The operator receives a scoped advisory record.
